reviews.details: Direct review traced the current ruleset identity from server creation through the live wire contract, client startup, presentation, replay validation and independently derived Loomkeeper plan. R6 shares the exact R5 volcanic terrain, opening positions and weapon table; only its named dynamics and compact target/presentation are selected. V8/V9 transition callers omit the new dynamics parameter and therefore retain their historical constants. Practice and Daily both bind to current R6, while PEI receipt and reward policy are unchanged. Waypoint 2 remains blocked on the owner's physical Phone Gate A correction acceptance.

Direct review confirms that current R6 alone replaces the dynamic thumbstick with compact translucent left, right and up/jump targets separated by three-pixel seams. A single captured pointer can slide through the cluster while preserving the last direction across each seam; direction changes remain bounded by the existing R6 authority and a fresh jump entry retains the 250ms landing buffer. A direct Jump entry now records neutral direction and launches with zero horizontal velocity without changing facing, while direction-to-Jump sliding records the last direction for takeoff. The V10 wire and replay contract accepts neutral jump only for current R6 authority; pre-R6 simulation and replay identities reject it. Pointer release, cancellation, lost capture and lifecycle boundaries retire local ownership. Threadleap, terrain, weapons, Practice/Daily identity, PEI and reward paths are unchanged. Physical Phone Gate A remains the acceptance boundary before Waypoint 2.

reviews.details: At committed and pushed 73e9aba, the owner reported that all five final physical-phone checks worked as expected: the translucent compact buttons and narrow spacing, neutral direct jump, directional slide-to-jump, repeated input, aftertouch and release behavior. Together with the previously accepted R6 presentation, pace, action clock and complete Practice turn journey, this closes Phone Gate A and authorizes Waypoint 2. It does not accept explosion impulse, Phone Gate B, complete Daily integration or package closure.

Direct review confirms that only current R6 supplies an impulse table and admits the new blast motion state. Damage distance and terrain exposure are calculated against intact terrain before deformation, then each exposed surviving actor receives deterministic radial motion; a coincident direct hit uses projectile travel direction rather than facing or input. Active and non-active actors share the existing swept collision, gravity, landing and bounded simulation-limit paths. Entering projectile and settling phases retires the authority lease and client pointer state; blast motion cannot consume player aftertouch, and the existing retreat restores the accepted controls. R5 has neither an impulse table nor a valid blast wire state, while crater, damage, projectile flight, Thread costs and reward/PEI policy are unchanged. Automated implementation acceptance is complete; physical feel and collision acceptance remain at Phone Gate B.
